newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Pick'n Pay jumps on results, bonus div.
newsitem.headline: Pick'n Pay jumps on results, bonus div.

text.p: Shares in South African stores group Pick'n Pay Ltd jumped on Wednesday following results that came in at the top of analysts' forecasts and a bonus dividend, dealers said.
The shares were unchanged before the results were announced at 1253 GMT and quickly put on 16 cents to hit a new year high of 590 cents by 1320 GMT.
"The results are good and the much higher dividend has given the stock a nice boost," one dealer said.
Pick'n Pay posted a year earnings per share of 29.33 cents, up from 22.55 cents last time. Analysts had predicted earnings on a range of 27.4 to 29.3 cents.
The firm also posted a dividend of 22.80 cents a share, up from 13.50 last time, that included a bonus 30th birthday dividend of five cents a share.
Analysts had predicted a dividend of 15.7 to 17.2 cents.
